subject: Dedicated capacity: recommended fleet mix (H100 / A100 / L4) for Medix Health
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Greene <susan.greene@medixhealth.com>, procurement@medixhealth.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — initial questions to size GPU fleet

Hi Susan / Medix procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. To make sure our Dedicated proposal gives you predictable latency and cost, can you confirm a couple of workload assumptions? If anything below is off, tell us and we’ll re-run the sizing:

- Primary model(s): are you planning to serve a 70B instruction-tuned model for conversational triage, plus smaller 13B models for clinical summarization?
- Average request length: ~300 input tokens and ~150 output tokens per call?
- Peak concurrent users: ~180 sessions during peak, average QPS estimated at 12 requests/sec (spiky pattern with 10–15x short bursts)?
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 300ms for the conversational flows.
- Data residency: US-only.

If confirmed, we’ll prepare a recommended fleet mix (H100 / A100 / L4) with expected throughput, EV (effective concurrent sessions per GPU), and a suggested burst pool. I’ll loop in Dev for the technical run-rates.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — quick answers below:

- Yes, main plan: 70B conv model for patient-facing chat, 13B summarization model for clinician notes, and embeddings for search.
- Request tokens: agree with your numbers (300 / 150).
- Peak concurrent users: 200 sessions peak; QPS can hit 18 for a short window (3–5 minutes).
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 250ms if possible for patient chat.
- Residency: US-only, support for SOC2 reports please.

Attaching our procurement template if you need it.

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Susan Greene <susan.greene@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — recommended fleet mix and tradeoffs

Hi all — ran the numbers against the workload assumptions (300/150 tokens, peak bursts to 18 QPS). Summary and recommendations below. I included assumptions used in capacity_model.xlsx (attached).

Key model characteristics impacting SKU choice:
- 70B conv model (dense transformer): best latency/throughput when served on large-memory GPUs to avoid OOMs for KV cache and long context. H100 80GB or A100 80GB recommended for single-GPU hosting of the 70B; A100 40GB requires 4-bit quantization and model-splitting strategies.
- 13B summarization: fits comfortably on A100 40GB or L4 with int8 quantization; good candidate to move to L4 for cost savings if you can accept slightly higher variability in tail latency.
- Embeddings: low-memory, high-throughput; L4 is vastly cheaper per embedding.

Performance & cost tradeoffs (high level):
- H100 (80GB) — best raw throughput and lowest latency for large-context models (70B). Ideal for P95 <= 250ms goal under heavy co-tenancy. Higher $/hour but reduces need for sharding and cross-GPU comms.
- A100 (80GB) — similar memory profile to H100 for 80GB SKUs; slightly lower perf on some kernels but widely available. Good balance for mixed workloads.
- A100 (40GB) — lower cost but requires aggressive quantization (4-bit) or model sharding for 70B; increases engineering complexity and can impact tail latency.
- L4 (48GB inference-optimized) — extremely cost-efficient for 13B and embedding workloads; great for high-throughput low-latency inference when models are quantized. Not recommended as the primary host for the 70B conv model at your desired SLO.

Suggested Dedicated fleet mix (baseline commit for steady-state + burst pool):
- Baseline: 4 x H100-80GB dedicated to the 70B conv model (pin a model version to this pool). This supports ~130–160 effective concurrent sessions with caching (prefix cache enabled) and gives headroom for P95 <= 250ms.
- Mid-tier: 6 x A100-80GB to host mixed 70B variants (can run smaller parallelism for off-peak) and support background batch tasks (summaries, backfills).
- Cost-sensitive layer: 12 x L4 nodes for embeddings, 13B summarization (quantized), and burst handling of low-cost paths. L4 handles the 18 QPS short bursts for 13B flows and embeddings.
- Burst pool: an on-demand pool of 4 A100-40GB (or 2 extra H100s if committed) to cover 5–10 minute traffic spikes.

Rationale & numbers (conservative):
- With our serving runtime and prefix/KV caching, an H100-80 typically delivers ~140–180 effective conversational sessions for the 70B model at target latency (P95 ~200–250ms) depending on request mix and cache hit rate.
- A100-80GB per-GPU session capacity is ~110–150 for same model; expect ~10–20% higher latency vs H100 in tight SLO scenarios.
- L4 for a quantized 13B: ~600–1,200 qps per node for short requests (small output sizes). Embedding throughput > 2,000 embeddings/sec per L4 depending on batch.
- Cost note: per-hour cost ratio (approx): H100-80 : A100-80 : A100-40 : L4 :: 4.5 : 3.2 : 1.8 : 0.5 (varies by region/providers).

Operational notes:
- We recommend pinning the 70B model to the H100 baseline pool to avoid noisy-neighbor tail effects.
- Enable automatic fallback routing: if H100 pool CPU completion starts to breach SLOs, route best-effort requests to A100 pool at slightly higher latency or to quantized variants.
- Reserve a small standby pool (burst) with faster autoscaling to handle 3–7 minute spikes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: If Medix grows faster than forecasted, the baseline may hit sustained saturation. Mitigation: staged commits (quarterly capacity add-ons) and pre-negotiated ramp credits.
- Risk: Quantization regression in clinical text quality for summarization. Mitigation: evaluate on your golden prompt set and enable a quality-guard rollback to A100 hosts.

Attachments: capacity_model.xlsx (contains per-GPU throughput simulations, cost estimates, and sensitivity sweeps).

Happy to run a tighter model-by-model simulation if you can share a sample of your token-length distribution and the exact 70B model variant.

— Dev
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Susan Greene <susan.greene@medixhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — recommended fleet mix and tradeoffs

Thanks Dev — this looks solid. A couple of commercial questions for procurement to consider:

1) Pricing/commits: propose a baseline 12-month commit covering the Baseline + Mid-tier plus a 6-month flex pool for L4. We’ll price the burst pool as an overlay (lower hourly reserve, higher burst rate).
2) SLA: we’ll include the SLA appendix (see sla-appendix.pdf) covering latency uptime and fallback obligations.
3) Migration cadence: plan a two-week trial run with canary traffic on H100 baseline before fully routing.

Susan — if Medix is ok with the commit structure, I can follow up with a formal proposal and the contract redlines.

— Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Susan — thanks for the clarity. Next steps / mutual action plan:

1) Medix: share a 48-hour sample of production request traces (anonymized) and golden prompts for the summarization model by Feb 26.
2) Redwood: run model-by-model perf sims and return an updated capacity_model.xlsx with per-GPU estimated P95s and cost bins by Mar 2.
3) Contract: Redwood to send a 12-month baseline + 6-month L4 flex commitment pricing sheet and SLA appendix by Mar 4.
4) Pilot: two-week canary on H100 baseline scheduled for week of Mar 15 (subject to contract).

I’ve attached the capacity_model.xlsx and the SLA appendix for review. If that sounds right, we’ll issue the formal proposal.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
